results.title: Customer Support AI Agent: What It Is & How It Works
results.content:
## What it should not handle

Most vendor content skips this section. It belongs here because accurate expectations are what make AI deployments sustainable.

Knowing where AI support fails is just as important as knowing what it can do.

Even with a well-built agent, some tickets will always need a human.

AI support agents work best on routine tickets with clear, documented answers. More complex, sensitive, or judgment-heavy cases should still move to a human.

That is not a failure. It is the design.

### High-emotion complaints

An AI agent can detect frustration and escalate.

It should not try to resolve situations where a customer is genuinely distressed. Someone who received a damaged product before an important event does not need a resolution path. [...] If starting from scratch, building the knowledge base comes before deploying the agent, not after.

### Your escalation design

Without defined escalation rules, handoff protocols, and context transfer, the deployment will frustrate customers rather than help them. This is where most deployments underdeliver.

Map it before going live.

If most of these are in good shape, a customer support AI agent is worth serious evaluation. If support volume is low or nearly every query requires specialist judgment, revisit it later.

At that point, compare the best customer support AI agents by how well they use your support knowledge, connect to the systems your workflows depend on, and transfer context when a human needs to take over. [...] Intent: what the customer wants to accomplish
 Entities: order number, account ID, product name, relevant dates
 Sentiment: frustrated, calm, confused, urgent
 Context: anything relevant from earlier in the same conversation

This is why an agent can take a message like "my package still hasn't shown up, and I ordered it a week ago" and understand it as a delivery tracking request tied to a specific account.

Not just a complaint to acknowledge and close.

### Layer 2: Decision

Once the agent knows what the customer needs, it figures out what to do. It draws on:

 The intent it identified
 Your business rules and policies
 The knowledge base it was trained on
 Any customer data it has access to

results.title: What Are the Most Common Complaints About AI Customer Support Tools? | Twig
results.content:
How to avoid it: Choose AI platforms that integrate deeply with your existing support stack. When your AI can pull customer history from Zendesk, order data from your commerce platform, and previous conversation context from your CRM, it can provide personalized, context-aware responses.

## Complaint 4: Responses Feel Robotic and Scripted

Customers can tell when they are talking to a poorly implemented AI. Overly formal language, generic responses that do not address the specific question, and rigid conversation flows all create an experience that feels more frustrating than helpful. [...] Key takeaways:

 Hallucinated or inaccurate answers are the number one complaint driving customer frustration
 Poor escalation to human agents traps customers in unhelpful AI loops
 Lack of context forces customers to repeat themselves across interactions
 Rigid, scripted responses fail to address nuanced customer issues
 Twig addresses these complaints through source-attributed accuracy and smart integration design

## Complaint 1: The AI Gives Wrong or Made-Up Answers

This is the most damaging complaint and the most common. AI hallucination, where the model generates plausible-sounding but factually incorrect information, is the fundamental trust-breaker in customer support. [...] How to avoid it: Choose tools that use retrieval-augmented generation with source attribution. When every AI response includes a citation to the source document, both customers and agents can verify the information. Twig was built specifically around this principle, ensuring that responses are always grounded in your actual documentation.

## Complaint 2: You Cannot Reach a Human When You Need One

Few things frustrate customers more than being trapped in an AI loop with no way to reach a human agent. This happens when AI tools are configured to minimize escalation at all costs, treating every human handoff as a failure rather than as an appropriate response to certain situations.
